subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If x = a(t − sin t) and y = a(1 + cos t), find d²y/dx².

mark_split.label: Differentiate both with respect to t
Form dy/dx and use half angles
Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t
Divide by dx/dt a second time

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how many times you divide by dx/dt, and why.

steps.label: Differentiate both with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both x and y are given through t, so nothing can be differentiated with respect to x directly. Get dx/dt and dy/dt first.

recall.must_convey: That dx/dt = a(1 − cos t) and dy/dt = −a sin t.
accept: differentiate x and y with respect to t first
dx by dt is a into one minus cos t
dy by dt is minus a sin t
modata rendintini t tho differentiate cheyyali
both are in terms of the parameter t

steps.why: This is a parametric pair, so every derivative with respect to x has to be built from derivatives with respect to t.
common_mistakes: Differentiating a(1 + cos t) as +a sin t.
Writing dx/dt as a(1 + cos t), copying the sign from y.
steps.memory_tip: In dx/dt the −sin t differentiates to −cos t, which builds the bracket 1 − cos t; in dy/dt the +cos t differentiates to −sin t.

steps.label: Form dy/dx and use half angles
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The half-angle forms are what make the next differentiation short: −cot(t/2) differentiates in one line, −sin t/(1 − cos t) does not.

lines.text: (this needs 1 − cos t ≠ 0, that is t not a multiple of 2π)

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx simplifies to −cot(t/2) using the half-angle forms.
accept: divide dy by dt by dx by dt to get minus cot t by two
use sin t equals two sin half t cos half t
one minus cos t is two sin squared half t
half angle formulas vaadithe minus cot t by two vasthundi
the a cancels and the twos cancel

steps.why: Leaving dy/dx as −sin t/(1 − cos t) forces a quotient rule at the next step. In the half-angle form it is a single cotangent.
common_mistakes: Writing 1 − cos t as 2 cos²(t/2), which is 1 + cos t.
Giving +cot(t/2) and losing the sign from dy/dt.
steps.memory_tip: 1 − cos t = 2 sin²(t/2) and 1 + cos t = 2 cos²(t/2) — the minus goes with the sine.

steps.label: Differentiate dy/dx with respect to t
steps.margin_note: Third mark. dy/dx is written in terms of t, so differentiate it with respect to t first; step 4 then divides by dx/dt. The ½ comes from the inner t/2.

lines.text: (dy/dx is a function of t, so differentiate it
the two minus signs give plus)

recall.must_convey: That differentiating −cot(t/2) with respect to t gives ½ cosec²(t/2).
accept: differentiate minus cot half t with respect to t
the derivative of cot is minus cosec squared so the two minus signs give plus
the chain rule on t by two gives a factor of half
cot differentiate cheste minus cosec square, rendu minus lu plus avuthai
the result is half cosec squared t by two

steps.why: dy/dx has been written in t, so this differentiation is with respect to t. The chain rule on the inner t/2 supplies the factor ½.
common_mistakes: Dropping the factor ½ from the inner t/2.
Giving −½ cosec²(t/2), keeping only one of the two minus signs.
steps.memory_tip: d/dt(cot u) = −cosec²u · du/dt; here u = t/2, so du/dt = ½.

steps.label: Divide by dx/dt a second time
steps.margin_note: Last mark. d²y/dx² is NOT d/dt(dy/dx). The chain rule needs a second division by dx/dt — write that division as its own line.

recall.must_convey: That d/dt(dy/dx) is divided by dx/dt a second time, giving d²y/dx² = cosec⁴(t/2)/(4a).
accept: divide by dx by dt a second time
d two y by d x squared is d by dt of dy by dx divided by dx by dt
the answer is cosec to the fourth of t by two over four a
rendo sari kooda dx by dt tho divide cheyyali
one over four a cosec fourth power t by two

steps.why: d²y/dx² means d/dx of dy/dx, and going from d/dt to d/dx needs another division by dx/dt. Do not stop one division early.
common_mistakes: Stopping at ½ cosec²(t/2) and calling it d²y/dx² — the second division by dx/dt is missing.
Dividing by dy/dt instead of dx/dt.
steps.memory_tip: One division for the first derivative, a second division for the second derivative — one dx/dt per order.

insider_note: The half-angle forms turn dy/dx into −cot(t/2). For the SECOND derivative divide by dx/dt again — differentiating with respect to t alone is the standard error here.
